data.hypothesis: The previously measured 256-thread tile was correct and faster than baseline, but its result does not isolate the tradeoff from tile size. A 128-thread CTA halves per-block shared memory to 3,584 bytes and may improve resource utilization, while also halving source reuse per tile and increasing tile iterations and barriers; measure whether any resource benefit offsets those costs. No speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: For this N-body kernel and protocol, the 256-particle shared tile is a useful measured reference, but its aggregate timing does not identify per-size behavior or the effect of tile size.
memory_lessons.claim: The 256-thread shared-tile candidate passed all correctness cases and measured 0.0009961626 seconds versus baseline 0.0018444100 seconds. This supports testing shared tiling but does not establish which tile size is best.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare a 128-thread, 128-source tile with the existing 256-thread configuration under the official protocol.

data.notes: This is a contrasting tile-size experiment, not a claim that the prior speedup generalizes. The prior 256-thread candidate (ba94d65d60514bb0) was valid at 0.0009961626 seconds; baseline-e1 was valid at 0.0018444100 seconds. The current candidate uses the same increasing source-interaction order, keeps inactive output threads participating in both barriers, stages only in-range source particles, and suppresses out-of-range writes. Controller correctness and timing remain authoritative.
transformations: Change CTA size and source-tile length from 256 to 128, with 3,584 bytes of dynamic shared memory for 128 Particle records.
Keep one target per thread and preserve ascending source-particle interaction order.
Retain block-wide barriers around tile consumption; all threads reach both barriers, including threads without valid output targets.
Handle partial source tiles and guard output writes for targets beyond n.
